I am exploring **generative AI and large language models as a productivity and engineering layer** for scientific computing, research, programming and workflow automation. The emphasis is **human-in-the-loop**: domain expertise remains responsible for scientific assumptions, model validity, numerical verification and interpretation.

::: {.panel .panel-accent}
**Credibility statement.** AI-generated code, models, statistics and scientific claims are treated as *assistive outputs* and require domain-expert review and independent validation before informing any scientific conclusion.
:::

## AI + pharmacology

Potential applications I am investigating sit firmly downstream of domain expertise: PK data-processing automation, pharmacometric workflow scaffolding, automated diagnostic plotting, simulation-workflow development, literature intelligence and reproducible-report generation, each requiring scientific verification before use.

## A responsible workflow

```{=html}
<div class="workflow">
  <span class="wf-step">Domain expertise</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">AI assistance</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Faster development</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Human review</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Scientific verification</span><span class="wf-arrow">→</span>
  <span class="wf-step">Reproducible result</span>
</div>
```

The value of AI here is speed and coverage, not authority. Scientific responsibility stays with the scientist.
